title: REPORT on the findings and recommendations of the Special Committee on the European Democracy Shield
part_text: 118. Underlines that the effectiveness and credibility of EU sanctions depend on strict and consistent enforcement; calls, therefore, on the Member States to establish a mechanism for the effective monitoring of enforcement activities, including through collaboration with civil society and academia, to improve coordination and to work together on closing loopholes and harmonising procedures; welcomes the fact that the announced revision of the mandate of the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) offers an opportunity to strengthen its role to include the investigation and prosecution of sanctions violations; stresses that the reform should be matched by adequate funding to enable the EPPO to effectively carry out its enhanced responsibilities; notes, however, that the effectiveness of sanctions depends on their consistent implementation by all state institutions and on the commitment of society as a whole, in particular companies and economic operators; strongly deplores the fact that, 12 years after Russia’s illegal annexation of Crimea and more than four years after the launch of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, thousands of European companies continue to operate on the Russian market, including more than 1 500 German companies, thereby generating revenues, taxes and economic capacity that contribute to Russia’s ability to sustain its war of aggression;
